name: Palazzo Firenze by Baglioni
positioning: Palazzo Firenze, an 18th-century noble residence in Florence's Santa Croce neighborhood, with frescoes and stuccoes alongside redesigned contemporary rooms
best_for: Travelers who want historic character with frescoed or coffered ceilings
Travelers who want to explore central Florence on foot

facts.text: The hotel occupies an 18th-century noble residence in Florence's Santa Croce neighborhood.
Inside, precious stuccoes, frescoes and original features meet high-end contemporary design.
Rooms and suites have been redesigned, each unique in character, proportion and detail.
Bathrooms in the rooms and junior suites are finished in Tuscan Breccia Capraia marble.
Deluxe rooms have Rubelli upholstery, dark parquet and custom-designed furniture.
Deluxe room amenities include Acqua di Parma bath amenities, an Illy coffee machine, a welcome bottle of wine and evening turn-down service.
Grand Deluxe Rooms have a shower with a Turkish bath.
The Two-Bedroom Family Junior Suite has two bedrooms with views of the Basilica of Santa Croce and two marble bathrooms.
The Two-Bedroom Santa Croce Royal Suite has coffered ceilings, original decorations and three marble bathrooms.
Attractions within walking distance include the Accademia Gallery, the Cathedral, Palazzo Vecchio, Ponte Vecchio and the Uffizi Gallery.
Guelfi and Ghibellini Restaurant serves Tuscan and Mediterranean cuisine by Chef Antonino Pepe, combining ancient recipes with modern techniques.
The whole palace can be reserved for weddings and private events.

highlights.text: A tour of the hotel reveals the Trestle of Santa Croce, an architectural feature once studied by Leonardo da Vinci.
The hotel hosts live music and intimate aperitivo concerts in its Music Room, among precious stuccoes.
Studio Marco Piva transformed the hotel's signature suites, pairing historic frescoes and decorated ceilings with custom-designed furnishings.
The Junior Suite Terrace has a balcony overlooking the rooftops and the Basilica of Santa Croce.
Some suites have original frescoed or coffered ceilings and views over the Basilica of Santa Croce or the streets of Santa Croce.

considerations.text: Deluxe and Grand Deluxe rooms look over the streets of Santa Croce or the internal courtyard; Basilica views are listed for some suites.
Small and medium-sized pets are welcome, for a supplement.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
